title: Who counts as a classic blues singer
summary: Asked what classic blues means, she names a few women she considers classic singers and calls Bessie Smith a barrelhouse singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Now you know in the 1920s, they referred to you -- they called you a classic blues singer.
Beautiful, just beautiful, Ms. Wallace, what would you call Sarah Martin? What kind of singer would you call her?
Well, she sing the blues. Blues.
You call her blues, classic blues?
How about Eva Taylor, what would you call her?

Well, she can, she can sing the blues. I saw Eva in New York. She tried -- Clarence made her a blues singer because he (unintelligible). And Eva then sing blues. She can sing blues like we can make you a blues singer. I'll make you a gospel singer, you (unintelligible).
I see. But some singers are more natural blues singers?
Some people, yeah. Some are more natural and some just comes out (unintelligible).
Who else, the way you see it, would you call a classic blues singer of the '20s? A real classic one that it came out that way, naturally? Who would you call -- which woman?
You might call her a classic singer. But (unintelligible). But you might could call Clara Smith.
Clara Smith? Yeah. And how about Victoria Spivey (PHONETIC).
So there weren't many classic blues singers.
Now there was you and Clara Smith?
And who else did you say?
Mamie Smith? She was a classic blues singer?
Uh-huh. And what's the other one? (Unintelligible). Who's that girl plays -- Kate Smith. Kate Smith got that Moon Over Miami. Kate Smith (unintelligible).
Oh, come on, you're kidding me now.
What kind of singer would you call Bessie Smith?
